author: Yellowpantstime
title: A Printing App That Makes Its Own Print Menu Unreadable
content:
This app is astonishingly bad at the one thing it is supposed to do: print.

On an iPhone in Dark Mode, the print-options menu can display white text on a white background, making the controls completely unreadable. That is not a minor cosmetic glitch. It makes the app functionally unusable. The official workaround is apparently to change the appearance setting for the entire phone just to use HP’s app, which is absurd.

HP has had ample time and resources to fix a basic interface defect that should never have passed quality control in the first place. Instead, customers who already paid for HP hardware are left troubleshooting an app that cannot reliably display its own menus.

A printer app should make printing easier. This one adds frustration, wastes time, and reflects an embarrassing lack of attention to basic usability.

content: The HP Printing App feels like it exists mostly to stand in the doorway and remind you that your printer would love to become a subscription service. However, after the recent update, I am facing a serious AirPrint issue. When I give a print command, the print does not come out. This problem does not appear to be related to the iPhone. It seems to be connected with the HP printer, Wi-Fi network connection, AirPrint connection, or the latest update.

I have already checked all the required settings, including Wi-Fi network, printer connection, HP Smart App, AirPrint support, printer online status, router, and iPhone settings. Both the iPhone and printers are connected to the same Wi-Fi network. These same settings were working properly earlier.

Therefore, HP should urgently look into this AirPrint issue caused after the recent update and provide a proper firmware/software update or technical solution. Regular HP customers are facing inconvenience because of this issue.

Overall Experience:
The printer quality is good, but after the recent update, the AirPrint problem is causing difficulty in daily use. I expect HP to resolve this issue as soon as possible.
